metadata.title: World Famous CHIRAWA PEDA, Rajasthan I Peda Factory + SAAG ROTA + Bade + Bawaliya Temple Visit
metadata.description:
Chirawa, a distinguished town in Rajasthan’s Jhunjhunu district, holds a special place in the Shekhawati region. This town is known for its strong ties to some of India’s most illustrious business families, including the Birlas, Dalmias, Khaitans, Poddars, Piramals, Singhanias, Goenkas, and Kanodias. 

Our food tour started with a visit to Pandit Ganesh Narayan’s Temple. This revered landmark offered us a glimpse into the spiritual and cultural fabric of the town, setting a serene tone for the day ahead.

Then, we headed to Lal Chand’s Peda Shop, renowned for its iconic peda. Here, we met Divyam, the third-generation owner, who shared stories about the shop’s rich legacy. He also introduced us to some of their other sweet delights, such as kali gajar paak and besan ki burfi. After sampling these treats, we headed to visit their peda-making unit, where we observed the labour-intensive process of making peda from scratch. The khoya prepared from scratch using both cow and buffalo milk was continuously stirred ensuring a smooth, creamy and lump-free texture. The peda’s toffee-like flavor and luscious texture left us in wonder. 

Next, we made our way to Malsaria Restaurant to indulge in saag rota, a classic winter dish. The robust cauliflower and green peas curry, cooked in desi ghee with over 16 spices, orange juice, and tomatoes, was rich and flavorful. Paired with a thick flatbread made from wheat flour and besan, this combination was quite a surprise.

Finally, we concluded our food tour at Ghanshyam Bade Wala, famous for its crisp lentil fritters called bada, made from moong and moth dal. We tasted both the crispy fried version and one soaked in fermented mustard-based water. These fritters, also offered as prasad at the temple. This was  a perfect finishing touch to our culinary journey through Chirawa.

Chirawa’s food scene is steeped in tradition and history that any food lover would cherish.
